title: One name for the button that shows and hides the properties panel
goal: The same button answers to three different names right now. Resting on it says Panel, the View menu calls it Show Layers, and until this morning it was called Inspector. A person who reads the menu and then looks for it on screen is hunting for the wrong word, and one of the scripted checks stopped working for exactly that reason. Pick one name and use it everywhere the panel is named.
notes: Filed by the 2026-09-07 digest design review. Evidence: audit queue/audits/2026-09-07-panel-toggle-titlebar.json, rough 3, which names all three words and says the menu was deliberately left alone because renaming it would touch the shipping release. That is the call to settle here rather than leave hanging. It has already cost something: Scripts/playtest/tool-tips.json fails at step 13 looking for Inspector (task the-tool-tips-walk-finds-the-panel-button-it-is). Files: Sources/Photonz/TitlebarPanelToggle.swift for the button, the View menu for Show Layers. Note the shortcut is Option Command L.
acceptance: The tooltip, the View menu row and any other place naming that panel all use one word
The word is the one the panel itself is called in the app, not a fourth invention
The shipping release is either left alone on purpose, with a line in the audit saying why, or changed with it
A scripted walk rests on the button and reads the name back
Audit written under queue/audits/ with a real capture of the button and the menu

log.note: Adversarial review before building. Three candidate words: Panel (the tooltip, and what every commit, task and audit calls it), Inspector (the Mac word, retired this morning), Layers (the View menu's Photoshop hangover). Layers is wrong on the facts: the column holds Layers, Library, Appearance, Measurement and whatever the tool in hand brings, so naming the whole thing after one section hides the rest. Inspector is wrong for the same reason in reverse: a Layers list and a Library shelf inspect nothing. Panel is what the thing is and what the app already says, so it wins and nothing has to be re-learned.

Shipping release: changed with it, on purpose. The button and the View menu are shared code, so current already said Hide Panel on the button and Show Layers in the menu, which is exactly the confusion this task was filed about. Leaving current alone would have left it in the release people use. Written up in the audit.

Shipped: PanelCopy in PhotonzCore is the one source (noun, menuItem, showTooltip, hideTooltip, controlName). MenuToggleNames.layersPanel -> .panel reads PanelCopy.menuItem; TitlebarPanelToggle reads the tooltips and the walk name from it. Feature descriptions in the Experiments window (FeatureCatalog, 9 strings) stopped calling it the inspector. menu-checkmarks-walk and docs/design/ui-building.md updated.

Verified: Scripts/test.sh green, 4381 tests. New Scripts/playtest/panel-name-walk.json rests on the button in both states and reads back "Hide Panel (⌥⌘L)" and "Show Panel (⌥⌘L)", dumps the View menu (Show Panel ⌥⌘L, unchanged key) and photographs it ticked and unticked. menu-checkmarks-walk passes with the new name. Screen Recording granted, so the audit carries real captures.
Left for its own task: Scripts/playtest/tool-tips.json line 21 still hovers "Inspector". That is the-tool-tips-walk-finds-the-panel-button-it-is, and it is now a one-word change to "Panel".

Panel is the one name. PanelCopy in PhotonzCore is the single source: the View menu row is Show Panel (was Show Layers), both tooltips are Show/Hide Panel, and the name a walk asks for all come from it. The Experiments window's feature copy stopped saying inspector. Option Command L unchanged; the shipping release got the rename too since the button and menu are shared, and the audit says why. Verified by Scripts/test.sh (4381 green), a new panel-name walk that reads the name back off the button and the menu, and menu-checkmarks. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-07-panel-one-name.json with real captures. Commit d3740119.
